subject.title: Feature: force media delivery as document attachment (e.g. #doc)

question: Should OpenClaw support a force-document behavior beyond the current per-call `forceDocument`/`asDocument` knobs, and if so should the public contract be `MEDIA:#doc`, a channel-level default, or something narrower?
rationale: The current code already solves explicit per-call sends, while the remaining request would create either new model-facing syntax or new channel config/default behavior that repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Keep per-call as canonical
options.body: Keep `--force-document` and `asDocument` as the supported contract for now and require a sponsored narrower proposal before adding syntax or config defaults.

options.title: Add `MEDIA:#doc` syntax
options.body: Define exact fragment parsing and media-kind semantics in the shared media pipeline, then thread it through affected channel delivery paths with tests and live proof.

options.title: Add channel default
options.body: Design a default-off per-channel/account setting, document upgrade behavior, and prove per-call override and existing default behavior remain intact.

recommendation.title: Keep per-call as canonical
recommendation.body: Keep `--force-document` and `asDocument` as the supported contract for now and require a sponsored narrower proposal before adding syntax or config defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about source-contract/config direction, and this person has the most recent current-line history across the relevant contract wording and delivery surfaces.
